clues.text: Reaching a top speed of 50 mph, this 102-foot-tall coaster sends riders upside down through 4 inversions.
This vintage steel looping coaster was built by Arrow and made its original debut in 1976.
This coaster can be found thrilling park visitors in the sunny state of California.
Following a major overhaul after the 1979 season, two of its original airtime hills were replaced by a pair of vertical loops, tying the world record for the most inversions at the time.
The name of this coaster refers to an evil supernatural spirit or fiend from the underworld.

evidence.quote: Demon is a looping roller coaster located at Six Flags Great America in Gurnee, Illinois and California's Great America in Santa Clara, California.
The two airtime hills were replaced with two vertical loops, bringing each ride's inversion count to four – tied for the most in the world at the time.
The backstory of the ride is that a demon slithered into Great America and attached himself to one of the ride's cars, then disappeared into the ride's structure.
